answer: Agent networks can resist Sybil attacks using photothermal challenge-response proofs. An agent energizes a micro-resistor into a glowing ember, measuring radiative decay through a saffron optical filter. Because physical imperfections govern the non-linear cooling curve, an adversary cannot forge valid telemetry in software and must deploy dedicated hardware per identity. However, thermal fatigue gradually shifts component baselines, causing sporadic false rejections.
